items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I was studying with Mrs. Pittman by then. She was a music teacher, yes... She said, 'Sammy, you have an exceptional knowledge of the instrument... you can share your feeling with other musicians who are trained.'

ctx.x: Yeah...well later by Mrs. Pittman,, Booker T. Washington's daughter. Later. But my first introduction to the piano was that lady asking me if I wanted to do some work for her. And I said yes. I don't know how that came out of my mouth, "Yes, I will, if you'll

let me play the piano." And then from that, I became big and bold. In 1923 the Charleston dance came out. And I became like an exceptional Charleston dancer. Now doing these dances, Danny, did one thing for me. It taught me to have confidence before an audience.
